target.title: fix(codex): prefer the pinned runtime for current models
target.body:
Closes #103884

## What Problem This Solves

Users selecting a newly supported Codex model could still get a “requires a newer version” failure when an older macOS desktop bundle shadowed the current Codex app-server packaged with OpenClaw. Switching between the pinned runtime and native Computer Use state also needed an exact, race-safe handoff so a thread could not load config under one executable owner and continue under another.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary managed Codex turns now prefer the pinned `@openai/codex` package. User-home and effective Computer Use configurations stay desktop-first because their native state and macOS permissions belong to that desktop runtime, with the pinned package retained as fallback when no desktop binary is available.

The handoff is bound to the exact spawned process identity and serialized inside one Gateway across native config-loading thread requests and Computer Use installation. Selection drift retires the old physical client and performs a bounded, replay-safe retry only when the request was proven not to have been written. Post-write cancellation or transport failure keeps the config fence through physical process exit and is never classified replay-safe.

Legacy one-off Computer Use identity flags now return literal-safe migration guidance for persistent `computerUse.pluginName` / `computerUse.mcpServerName` configuration. Explicit app-server command overrides remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Current Codex models use the OpenClaw-pinned runtime by default even when an older desktop app is installed. Computer Use continues to run under the desktop app that owns its local permissions and persisted native state. CLI status/install guidance preserves custom identities and marketplace arguments exactly.

The native-config fence coordinates one running Gateway process. After another Codex process or Gateway changes native plugin config, restart the Gateway and start a new chat before relying on the new selection.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx7j9nwct0kgxr6nynkzjafp`: 516 focused Codex extension tests passed, plus 17 embedded-runner app-server recovery tests.
- Blacksmith Testbox: `pnpm tsgo:extensions` passed on the final snapshot.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Structured Codex autoreview and a separate focused lifecycle review reported no accepted/actionable P1 or compile findings after the final replay-safety fix.
- Upstream Codex source was inspected for initialize identity, native config loading on thread start/resume/fork, plugin-install persistence, npm launcher/platform-package selection, and app-server CLI config semantics. The fix selects and tracks the real executable rather than spoofing `clientInfo.version`.

AI-assisted change; implementation and validation were reviewed by the maintainer agent.

target.title: fix(feishu): prevent long streaming replies from draining stale updates
target.body:
Closes #91941

AI-assisted: this fix was developed and reviewed with an AI coding assistant. I understand the implementation and verified the queue/lifecycle behavior described below.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu/Lark users receiving long streaming-card replies could wait minutes after model generation had completed because every intermediate full-content snapshot remained queued for delivery.

The previous cadence-only candidate, #91943, was closed after a live cadence experiment did not materially improve the multi-minute tail. This change removes the separate dispatcher FIFO and relies on the existing `FeishuStreamingSession` queue, which already coalesces pending full-content snapshots.

## Why This Change Was Made

`FeishuStreamingSession` is now the single owner of streaming update ordering:

- The reply dispatcher forwards snapshots directly to `session.update()` instead of serializing every snapshot in a second `partialUpdateQueue`.
- While one CardKit request is blocked, the session's existing `pendingText` state replaces stale intermediate snapshots with the latest cumulative text.
- The session's existing `close()` and `discard()` paths set `closed`, clear the throttle timer, and await the same internal queue before finalizing.
- Dispatcher-side update rejections are logged without creating another queue or lifecycle state machine.

This keeps the existing 160 ms CardKit update cadence and full-content payload contract unchanged.

## User Impact

Long Feishu/Lark streaming replies no longer need to replay every stale dispatcher snapshot after generation finishes. The card converges to the latest complete answer using the existing session-owned queue, without introducing a second source of truth for close/discard ordering.

## Evidence

### Live Feishu behavior proof

This was validated in real Feishu use by the operator who reproduced the original latency problem, not only through mocked/unit-test boundaries.

- **Before this patch:** a long streaming reply continued visibly revealing queued full-content snapshots for several minutes, even after model generation had completed.
- **After deploying this patch and restarting the Gateway:** the streaming card kept pace with model output and completed at approximately the same time as generation (about **15 seconds** in the observed run), with no multi-minute post-generation drain tail.

The timing is an operator-observed, real-tenant before/after rather than a synthetic benchmark; message content and tenant identifiers are intentionally omitted.

#### Exact revision used for the live deployment

The OpenClaw instance used for this live Feishu test ran the Feishu implementation from PR commit `b614742e1ed283674e7784789ff39ce3af428587`.

### Blocked-request behavior proof

The tests exercise both sides of the ownership boundary:

- **Dispatcher ownership:** while the first mocked session update is blocked, later snapshots are still forwarded immediately; the dispatcher does not serialize or buffer them.
- **Session latest-wins:** with the first real `FeishuStreamingSession` CardKit request blocked, a three-snapshot burst emits only the first and latest request bodies; the stale middle snapshot is not sent.
- **Close drain:** `close()` does not send CardKit settings/finalization until the blocked update settles, then sends the latest final text.
- **Discard drain:** `discard()` does not delete the card until the blocked update settles.

```console
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run \
    extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts \
    extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       115 passed (115)
```

### Extension verification

```console
$ node scripts/test-extension.mjs feishu
Test Files  77 passed (77)
Tests       1107 passed (1107)

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check \
    extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts \
    extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts \
    extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs \
    --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json \
    extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts \
    extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts \
    extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.

$ git diff --check origin/main
# no output
```

### Scope and limitations

- The live result is a real Feishu tenant observation with approximate wall-clock timing, not a lab-grade packet trace.
- Full repository `pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test` was not run locally; CI remains the broad validation gate.

### Independent review

```console
$ codex review --base origin/main
No actionable regressions were found. The dispatcher now delegates concurrency to the existing session-owned queue, whose close and discard paths wait for in-flight updates; the added tests cover overlapping updates and terminal-operation ordering.
```

target.title: fix: keep yielded parent runs deferred until subagents settle
target.body:
## Summary

This change promotes yielded-parent semantics into a shared parent lifecycle classifier and routes the affected cron, subagent-registry, and Discord/source-message paths through that state instead of letting each consumer infer completion from terminal-shaped model-attempt events, missing final text, or abort-shaped control flow.

The shipped behavior is:

- yielded parent + active descendants is treated as waiting/deferred, not ordinary completion;
- yielded parent + no descendant is treated as diagnostic error;
- cron delivery waits for a real final outcome instead of counting the yielded attempt as `ok / not-delivered`;
- Discord/source-message progress remains parent-owned while the yielded parent is waiting;
- descendant settlement wakes/reconciles yielded parents through the existing continuation paths.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where parent-agent runs that spawned child sessions/subagents and then called `sessions_yield` could look finished before the parent task actually completed.

The most visible failures were:

- isolated cron `agentTurn` jobs with valid delivery targets could finish as `ok / not-delivered` because the yielded parent had no final payload yet;
- Discord source-message lifecycle could clear parent progress/done indicators while child work was still active or while the parent was waiting to reconcile final output;
- run history/status surfaces made yielded parent work look like delivery failure, ordinary success with no output, or completed source-message work instead of a paused/resumable parent lifecycle.

`session_yield` is supposed to end the current model turn, not the parent task. This PR makes that distinction explicit for the affected runtime consumers.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

Operators and developers can now rely on `sessions_yield` after spawning child/subagent work without the parent run being misrepresented as complete at the cron or Discord lifecycle boundary.

Practically:

- autonomous development crons stop inflating misleading `ok / not-delivered` results for intentionally yielded runs;
- cron history exposes a distinct `deferred` state for yielded parent handoff;
- Discord progress no longer marks the parent source message done just because the parent yielded while children continue;
- yielded parent runs are resumed/reconciled when descendant work settles;
- debugging points to the parent/child lifecycle state instead of falsely implying delivery target resolution failed.

## Linked Context

- #95535 — `sessions_yield` isolated cron resumption/delivery gap.
- #92369 — subagent orchestration in isolated cron sessions needs reliable spawn/wait/aggregate semantics.
- #92116 — `sessions_yield` completion delivered as passive context can break orchestration loops.
- #86537 — subagent terminal reconciliation can expire suspended final delivery.
- #86538 — session write-lock timeouts can block subagent delivery lanes.
- #95833 — subagent abort-settle/session-lock failure can break session continuation.
- #92460 — isolated cron completion delivery gap around final controller return.
- #95604 — Discord subagent progress visibility.
- #94153 — durable queued subagent completion announcements.
- #95847 — requester-consumed descendant completion accounting.

## What Changes

### Shared parent lifecycle state

- Adds `src/agents/agent-lifecycle-parent-state.ts`.
- Classifies lifecycle events with explicit yielded/waiting vs terminal semantics.
- Exports the classifier through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime`.
- Routes subagent registry and Discord source-message handling through the classifier instead of local `yielded && paused` inference.

### Cron lifecycle and delivery

- Adds first-class cron run status `deferred`.
- Classifies yielded descendant handoff before delivery-mode branching, so text, structured payloads, `delivery.mode: none`, source-satisfied delivery, and normal direct delivery all share the same semantics.
- Prevents duplicate/interim parent announcements while descendants are active.
- Records yielded-without-descendant as explicit error diagnostic.
- Keeps deferred manual task runs active rather than failing them.
- Disables one-shot deferred cron jobs after handoff to avoid retry loops.

### Persistence, protocol, CLI, and UI

- Extends run-log JSON/SQLite encoding and status filtering for `deferred`.
- Extends Gateway protocol schemas and cron server filters.
- Extends CLI status/wait typing and docs.
- Extends hook-visible status typing.
- Adds Control UI status/filter labels and generated locale fallbacks.

### Parent/subagent reconciliation

- Tracks yielded/paused parents that still have pending descendants.
- Marks yielded parents with `wakeOnDescendantSettle` so they are resumed/reconciled when descendant work settles.
- Handles child success/failure settlement through existing subagent lifecycle recovery paths.
- Adds regression coverage for yielded parents being reconciled after child failure so diagnostics can wake the parent.

### Discord/source-message lifecycle

- Projects lifecycle events from agent execution into reply/channel handling.
- Uses the shared classifier to identify yielded/waiting parent state.
- Preserves in-progress/progress representation for yielded parents with active children.
- Avoids prematurely marking Discord status reactions done or clearing draft/progress state when the parent yielded and remains waiting.

### Concurrent user-message semantics

`docs/tools/subagents.md` documents the selected policy: if a human sends another message while a requester is yielded, the new message starts a normal turn for the same requester session. OpenClaw keeps the yielded run visible as waiting on descendant completion rather than converting it into a stale final reply; when descendant completion arrives, the completion event is handed back to the requester for synthesis.

## Implementation Notes

Implementation details are included in the What Changes section above; focused evidence and live behavior proof are preserved below.

## Tests / Verification

Focused test coverage plus type, docs, and formatting gates are preserved under Evidence below.

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)
- Previous PR head: `c163d18fa610687e7dfb8585f1fe8f30b0c4185d`
- Current PR head: `73cff6aa1b0a3ab5786fdfc3a96c98f575e7fcc8`
- Rebased and squashed to one commit on the common base; pushed with `--force-with-lease`.

### ClawSweeper Requested Real Behavior Proof Coverage

ClawSweeper requested redacted live behavior proof for the yielded-parent/deferred lifecycle across the surfaces touched by this PR. This body currently includes the live cron/subagent deferred handoff proof below: a real Dev-01 cron run where the yielded parent remained `deferred` while a descendant was active, with redacted run output, child completion marker, and run/shared-state checks.

Remaining ClawSweeper-requested proof not present in this body yet:

- Redacted Discord visual status/progress/status-reaction proof showing a yielded parent with active descendants remains visibly in progress until descendant settlement.
- Best-effort cron yielded handoff proof/regression after the `deliveryBestEffort` bypass fix, showing best-effort delivery does not incorrectly bypass the yielded-parent deferred lifecycle.
- Migration/upgrade compatibility proof for the detected persistent data-model/status-contract changes.

Maintainer acceptance is still needed for the public `deferred` cron/status/SDK contract; that is a review decision, not something runtime proof alone can certify.

### Real / Live Behavior Proof

The non-zero wait exit is expected for this proof: `openclaw cron run --wait` exits non-zero for persisted `deferred` status, while still returning the run record. Follow-up inspection showed the spawned child completed with marker `CHILD_MARKER pr95996-95847-live-20260623T222458Z` and the shared state row recorded `ended_reason = subagent-complete`. The cron shared-state row for the same job persisted `last_run_status = deferred`, `last_delivery_status = not-requested`, and diagnostic summary `cron isolated agent yielded while descendant runs are still active`.

Proof sources:

Remaining proof gap: this live proof covers the cron yielded-parent/subagent deferred lifecycle path. It does not provide Discord visual status-reaction proof.

### Focused test coverage

```bash

  src/agents/agent-lifecycle-parent-state.test.ts \

Coverage includes:

target.title: fix(codex): preserve UTF-16 pairs in tool output delta truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `CodexAppServerEventProjector` tool output delta streaming produces a lone high surrogate when a non-BMP character (emoji) straddles the `remainingChars` truncation boundary. The `.slice(0, remainingChars)` call on line 1447 cuts at a UTF-16 code unit boundary, and when the cut point lands on a HIGH surrogate whose paired LOW surrogate falls just beyond the limit, the truncated chunk ends with a dangling `\uD83D`-style byte that corrupts tool output display.

## Why This Change Was Made

`truncateUtf16Safe` is already imported on line 29 and used elsewhere in the same file (lines 3413, 3435) — this single call site was missed. The fix replaces `.slice(0, remainingChars)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(delta, remainingChars)`, using the same canonical helper.

## User Impact

Streaming tool output from Codex app-server sessions no longer risks rendering corrupted surrogate bytes when model-generated tool output contains emoji characters near the output size limit boundary. No user-visible impact for ASCII-only tool output.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** The 8,000-char `TOOL_PROGRESS_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS` progress-message cap can split a non-BMP character's surrogate pair when `remainingChars` lands on the HIGH surrogate. The fix uses `truncateUtf16Safe` to back off before the surrogate pair.

**Real environment tested:** Node.js v22.22.0, x64, linux

### 1. Production module proof (truncateUtf16Safe from packages/normalization-core)

The proof script imports the real production `truncateUtf16Safe` — no reimplementation:

```
node --import tsx proof-codex-event-projector-utf16.mjs
```

**Evidence after fix:**
```
=== POSITIVE (fix: truncateUtf16Safe from production module) ===

module: packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.js
[c1] remaining=1, delta=😀hello (surrogate split)  chars=7999/8000 deltaCount=2
  ok: no lone surrogates
[c2] remaining=2, delta=😀 (exactly fits)  chars=8000/8000
  ok: emoji intact
  ok: no lone surrogates
[c3] remaining=2, delta=x😀y (cut at HIGH surrogate)  chars=7999/8000
  ok: no lone surrogates
  ok: emoji excluded cleanly
[c4] ASCII: remaining=10, delta=10 chars  chars=8000/8000
  ok: chunks clean
```

**Negative control (pre-fix behavior reproduced in the same script):**
```
=== NEGATIVE (old: .slice(0, remainingChars)) ===

[n1] remaining=1, delta=😀hello  chars=8000/8000
  BUG: lone surrogate U+D83D at [0] "\ud83d"
  ok: bug reproduced (lone surrogate emitted)
[n2] remaining=2, delta=x😀y (cut after HIGH, before LOW)  chars=8000/8000
  BUG: lone surrogate U+D83D at [1] "x\ud83d"
  ok: bug reproduced (lone surrogate emitted)

=== Summary ===
node=v22.22.0 MAX=8000 source=production truncateUtf16Safe
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 8 passed, 0 failed

### 2. Real CodexAppServerEventProjector regression test (vitest)

target.title: fix(gateway): align runtime config activation with subsystem hot-reload publish (#103736)
target.body:
Closes #103736

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a gateway config hot reload that changes hooks, cron, and channel settings simultaneously leaves the process in a mixed state for up to 5 minutes when a channel restart is deferred waiting for active work to drain. During that window, `getRuntimeConfig()` already returns the new configuration while hook routing still resolves against the old hooks config and `deps.cron` points at the old (already stopped) cron instance.

This means a hook request arriving mid-window is routed to the wrong agent or session, and a cron job created or deleted in that window can be silently ineffective.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause has two independent parts, each requiring its own move:

1. `onHotReload` commits the runtime config snapshot (`activate: true`) *before* `applyHotReload` runs, so `getRuntimeConfig()` advances while subsystem state stays on the old references through deferral.

2. `applyHotReload` stops and replaces the cron service *before* entering the channel-restart deferral loop, so `deps.cron` points at a stopped instance for up to 5 minutes.

This fix makes two narrow relocations — no new callback, no secrets-lock refactor, no `onActivated`:

- **Move 1 (config + auth):** `onHotReload` uses `activate: false` (prepare only), then the real `activate: true` call moves to after `applyHotReload` returns, right after `setState`. Auth-session generation advances together with the commit, so `getRuntimeConfig()`, hooks routing, and session generation never diverge.

- **Move 2 (cron):** The `restartCron` block (stop → build → start) is moved from before the channel-restart deferral to immediately before `setState`. The old cron stays live and reachable through `deps.cron` throughout the deferral window; `setState` atomically publishes the replacement.

This approach is **symmetric with #100586** (which fixed the noop path by committing a missing snapshot). That PR also used a narrow relocation without refactoring the reload lifecycle machinery. This PR does the same for the hot path: move the commit to the right place; don't touch the lifecycle machine.

**Scope exclusions** (explicitly left as follow-ups, mirroring #100586's narrow scope):

- `heartbeatRunner.updateConfig`, `applyGatewayLaneConcurrency`, `refreshContextWindowCache`, `channelHealthMonitor.stop` remain in their original positions (before deferral), matching the "less user-visible" assessment in the issue description. These produce an old-config/new-runner window that is not addressed here — a dedicated follow-up PR can move them similarly if needed.

- No overlap with #103880: that PR took a publish-early approach (restructuring `applyHotReload` with a try/catch rollback wrapper). This PR takes the commit-align direction, which is the root cause described in the issue. It is a single-file change with no new API surface and no structural refactor.

## User Impact

Operators running busy gateways with hooks and cron will see consistent behavior during a config hot reload: hook routing, `deps.cron`, `getRuntimeConfig()`, and session generation all observe either the old or the new configuration together, never a mix. Cron RPCs during deferred channel restarts always target a live (old) service.

## Evidence

**Tests:**
```
✓ src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts — 60 passed (2 new)
✓ src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts — 348 passed
✓ TypeScript (tsc --noEmit) — clean
✓ oxlint — 0 warnings, 0 errors
```

**Real behavior proof (standalone harness, `node --import tsx`):**
```
 SCENARIO 1: old cron stays live through deferral
  [PASS] old cron was stopped during reload
  [PASS] deferral was entered
  [PASS] hooks stayed at old value throughout
 RESULT: ALL ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

**New test — cron liveness:** `does not stop the old cron until after the channel-restart deferral drains` — drives the real `createGatewayReloadHandlers` / `applyHotReload` with `hoisted.activeEmbeddedRunCount` and fake timers, verifying `oldCron.stop` is called 0 times during deferral and 1 time after drain.

**New test — commit-after-publish:** `defers runtime snapshot commit until after subsystem state is published` — verifies `setState` completes before any config commit would happen.

**Error recovery:** Existing test `resets context metadata after a managed hot reload rolls back` continues to pass — the original catch-block semantics are unchanged since `activate: false` never committed the snapshot before the try block.

**Verification checklist:**
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts` — 60 passed (28 + 28 existing + 2 new)
- `pnpm test src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts` — 348 passed
- `pnpm tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `pnpm oxlint src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.ts` — 0 errors
- `node --import tsx fix-103736-real-behavior-proof.mjs` — all assertions passed

--- 

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using AI tools (opencode) with review by the author.

target.title: feat(plugin-sdk): re-export StatusSummary, SessionStatus, and HeartbeatStatus from command-status
target.body:
## Summary

Adds three additive type re-exports to the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status` entrypoint so plugins consuming gateway status RPCs (or formatting `/status` output) can bind against the canonical host shape:

- `StatusSummary` (top-level `/status` payload)
- `SessionStatus` (per-session row inside `summary.sessions.recent[]` / `summary.sessions.byAgent[].recent[]`)
- `HeartbeatStatus` (per-agent heartbeat status)

`ModelCatalogEntry` is already exposed via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-runtime` (re-exported from `agents/model-catalog.js`) — kept as-is.

## Why

From the issue: an external plugin (`lossless-claw#516`) navigated `sessions.byAgent[].entries[].usage.{promptTokens, totalTokens, input}` against `StatusSummary` — but the actual shape is `sessions.byAgent[].recent[]` keyed by `key`. The plugin's `pickFirstNumber` would have returned `null` on every field. Root cause: the author had no public type to import and was guessing the shape from the slash-command formatted output. Even after a typed gateway-RPC client lands, this drift will recur if the type isn't on the public surface.

## Changes

- `src/plugin-sdk/command-status.ts` — Add `export type { HeartbeatStatus, SessionStatus, StatusSummary } from "../commands/status.types.js";` with a comment pointing at the issue.
- `src/plugin-sdk/command-status.types.test.ts` — Regression test that imports each type and assigns from a sample literal so a future rename of the host type breaks here loudly.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — `Unreleased > Changes` entry.
- `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` — Regenerated via `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:gen`; `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` is green.

Per `src/plugin-sdk/CLAUDE.md`: additive, backwards-compatible, narrow. Reuses the existing `command-status` entrypoint rather than introducing a new subpath. No runtime code; types only, so no startup-cost impact and nothing for the entrypoint profiler to flag.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/command-status.types.test.ts` — 1/1 pass
- [x] `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:gen` — regenerated baseline
- [x] `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` — `OK docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256`
- [x] `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on touched files — clean

Refs #76759.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Closes #76759. Plugin authors building command-status integrations needed access to `StatusSummary`, `SessionStatus`, and `HeartbeatStatus` types from the public Plugin SDK, but those types were not re-exported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status`. Without these exports, plugins had to either copy the type definitions (drift risk) or import from internal paths (boundary violation). This PR adds the type-only re-exports.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout at HEAD `b8bc8423d2` on Node 22 / Darwin 25.2.0, exercising the production Plugin SDK type-only re-export path through `src/plugin-sdk/command-status.ts` and the public package exports surface. The regression test imports the types from `./command-status.js` (the same module a plugin author would consume) and uses them in real declared shapes; no mocks of the SDK boundary under test.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/command-status.types.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` from the repository root, compiling via tsgo (which type-checks the import) and asserting the imported types can be used as the actual `SessionStatus`, `HeartbeatStatus`, and `StatusSummary` shapes a plugin would build.
- **Evidence after fix:** Captured terminal output from the `pnpm` invocation above on this exact branch:

  ```
   RUN  v4.1.5 /Users/shubh-trips/Documents/personal-project/open-source/openclaw

   ✓ |unit-fast| src/plugin-sdk/command-status.types.test.ts > command-status type re-exports (#76759) > StatusSummary, SessionStatus, and HeartbeatStatus are importable as types 1ms

   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  1 passed (1)
     Duration  74ms
  ```

  Runtime assertions captured by the live import: (a) `StatusSummary`, `SessionStatus`, and `HeartbeatStatus` are importable as types from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status`; (b) declaring concrete values of each shape compiles and runs through tsgo type-checking; (c) the outer `StatusSummary` shape includes `tasks` and `taskAudit` slots that consumers can fill with the documented internal types via cast (no leak of internal types).
- **Observed result after fix:** Third-party plugin authors can `import type { StatusSummary, SessionStatus, HeartbeatStatus } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status"` and build status-integration plugins without copying type definitions or reaching into core. Pre-fix on the same install: this import threw a TS error because the symbols were not re-exported from the SDK barrel.
- **What was not tested:** Runtime behavior of plugins consuming these types — the PR is type-only (`export type {...}`); there is no runtime code surface to exercise.

target.title: RFC: add local adaptive-refresh replay tooling
target.body: ## Decision requested This RFC asks whether upstream should own a local replay harness for Adaptive refresh and, if so, whether the pure replay tools should be separated from runtime trace collection and the coding-activity probe. It does not change the production policy or make Adaptive the default. The decision record in #1739 requires measured evidence before a default change, and #1861 shipped the current opt-in policy. This branch adds tooling to collect and audit that evidence. Refs #1739 and #1861. ## What is in the branch - `AdaptiveReplayKit`, a Foundation-only library for parsing traces, replaying policies, segmenting unobserved gaps, calculating metrics, and auditing recorded schedule decisions. - `AdaptiveReplayCLI`, a thin command-line wrapper around the library. - An off-by-default app recorder for policy decisions, menu opens, refresh completions, and accepted or rejected timer-advance evaluations. - A shadow-mode coding-activity probe that reads metadata from recent local Codex and Claude Code transcripts. Its signal is never passed to the production policy. - A replay-only candidate that caps unconstrained decisions at five minutes while recent coding activity is present. ## Diff shape Relative to `main`, this is 32 files with 4,147 insertions and 55 deletions. It is a large review surface, so the table separates runtime wiring from the offline harness and its tests. | Surface | Files | Insertions / deletions | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Feature tests | 10 | +1,932 / -0 | | Offline replay library and CLI | 13 | +1,619 / -1 | | App wiring, recorder, and activity probe | 6 | +417 / -6 | | Docs | 2 | +132 / -6 | | Keychain test isolation | 1 | +47 / -42 | The keychain test change wraps an existing suite in no-UI test overrides so the full validation does not read real credentials; its net change is five lines. If upstream wants a smaller sequence, the natural split is replay kit and CLI, runtime recording, then the activity probe and replay-only candidate. ## Local data boundary Tracing is disabled unless the `adaptiveRefreshTraceEnabled` defaults key is set. When enabled, the app appends JSONL records in its Application Support directory. The writer has a hard 10 MiB cap and stops before a record would exceed it; it does not rotate, truncate, or upload the file. The activity probe reads file metadata only: modification time, creation time, size, and the number of recently modified transcripts. It does not read transcript contents or store file paths, project names, account information, credentials, provider responses, or menu content. There is no network or analytics path for these records. The raw trace used below remains local and is not part of this PR. The decision record now proposes the exact file location, manual disable/delete commands, and a one-traced-process-per-file constraint. There is no retention or deletion UI; accepting that boundary is one of the decisions requested by this RFC. ## Replay evidence The frozen single-machine trace contains 1,780 records (SHA-256 `b1e4aa33180b7c177293eb9ed16b45e24e026d259600fba2b1b67b931b904f0b`). The legacy-gap heuristic split it into 28 observed segments and excluded 26.10 hours of unobserved wall time. This is not a causal classification: the trace cannot distinguish sleep or reboot from a long refresh or event-loop stall. Activity metadata was available for 462 of 733 recorded decisions. Of those 462 samples, 185 were inside the five-minute active window. | Policy | Simulated refreshes | Per observed 24h | Simulated advances | Unconstrained active over 5m | Menu staleness p50 / p95 | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Current Adaptive | 694 | 143.47 | 53 | 4 / 145 | 142s / 1093s | | Activity-cap candidate | 696 | 143.88 | 53 | 0 / 145 | 139s / 1093s | | Fixed 5m | 1,383 | 285.90 | 0 | 0 / 99 | 150s / 281s | On this trace, current Adaptive scheduled 49.8% fewer simulated refreshes than the fixed five-minute baseline. The replay-only candidate added two refreshes, removed the four active-delay violations, and reduced p50 menu staleness by three seconds. It did not improve p95. The fixed five-minute baseline had a p95 menu staleness of 281 seconds, compared with 1,093 seconds for both Adaptive variants. This trace therefore supports the scheduled-work reduction but does not support making Adaptive the default. The frozen trace predates the new evaluation event. It contains 46 recorded timer advances and zero timer-advance evaluations, so it cannot validate accepted versus rejected live comparisons. A short instrumented run of the equivalent pre-rebase patch series produced two evaluation records, one accepted decision, and zero payload, decision, or menu-link mismatches. That checks the audit path; it is not additional statistical evidence. These numbers count simulated refreshes and observed menu staleness on one machine. They do not measure battery savings, user time saved, provider API requests, or cost. ## Validation Exact candidate: `2d43edbb781fa520357c75fd6938f68d55e93bc4` - `make check` passed, including SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint. - `make test` passed all 604 selections across 51/51 groups. - Focused replay, parser, trace-recording, segmentation, audit, and activity runs passed 83 tests in 10 suites. This includes the byte-cap/oversized-record cases and one-to-one menu/evaluation linkage. - `swift build --product AdaptiveReplayCLI` passed. - JSON schema smoke checks passed for raw-wall-clock and segmented runs, including audit validity and segmentation provenance. - `CODEXBAR_SIGNING=adhoc ./Scripts/package_app.sh debug` produced a bundle for this exact commit; `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passed. ## Known limitations - The measured trace comes from one machine. - Legacy gap segmentation is heuristic, not causal. - The raw trace is intentionally not published. - Older frozen records cannot audit rejected timer-advance evaluations. - There is no retention or deletion UI yet. - Trace writes and the 10 MiB boundary are serialized within one process; concurrent traced instances sharing the file are unsupported. - This evidence makes no battery, elapsed-user-time, API-request, cost, or default-policy claim. ## Review questions 1. Should the pure replay kit and CLI live in this repository? 2. Should runtime trace recording be reviewed separately? 3. Is the stat-only coding-activity probe acceptable upstream, or should it remain out of tree? 4. What retention and deletion contract is required before persistent traces can ship? This PR does not propose a new production policy, persistent analytics, a default change, or use of the activity signal at runtime.

target.title: Split provider pane settings into Menu bar and Connection sections
target.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #2047. Provider detail panes had a single vague "Settings" section mixing the menu-bar metric picker with connection controls. This splits it into two topical sections:

- **Menu bar** — the shared menu-bar metric picker, Copilot's secondary-metric picker, and Kiro's menu-bar value picker
- **Connection** — usage/auth-source pickers, cookie-source pickers, API-region pickers, the Claude keychain prompt policy, JetBrains IDE selection, and action rows (Google OAuth, Gemini CLI migration)

Implemented via a `placement` field on `ProviderSettingsPickerDescriptor` defaulting to `.connection`, so only the three menu-bar pickers declare a placement and no other provider code changes. A full inventory of all 44 picker IDs confirmed the classification.

Deliberately unchanged: the header-less identity card (a header would duplicate the provider name), "Usage", "Quota warnings", and "Options" — the residual toggles ("Battery Saver", "OpenAI web extras", "Avoid Keychain prompts", …) are genuinely heterogeneous, so a topical header there would mislead.

## Localization

Both new headers translated into all 22 non-English catalogs; the orphaned `"Settings"` key removed everywhere; strict locale parity checks unchanged and green.

## Testing

- `make check` clean (locale parity, SwiftFormat, SwiftLint strict); `make test` full suite green
- New/extended tests: placement assertions for the shared metric picker, Copilot secondary metric, Kiro menu-bar display, and representative connection pickers

_Replaces #2049, which was auto-closed when its head branch was briefly deleted during a merge-conflict repair; the branch has since been rebased onto the 0.42.0 release prep._

target.title: fix(browser): refresh target after guarded existing-session actions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Existing-session `hover`, `scrollIntoView`, `drag`, `select`, and `fill` actions already run the post-interaction navigation guard, but their success responses kept the pre-action `targetId`. If one of those guarded actions triggered a renderer swap or same-URL target replacement, the next browser action could continue with a stale target.

## Why This Change Was Made
`click`, `clickCoords`, `type`, and `press` already resolve the current target after the same guarded existing-session path. This change applies that same response contract to the remaining guarded non-click interactions without changing unguarded or unsupported actions.

## User Impact
Browser agents using existing-session profiles get the current tab target after guarded hover, scroll, drag, select, and fill interactions. This reduces stale-target follow-up failures after navigation-like page changes.

## Evidence
- Added a regression test that simulates a guarded non-click interaction replacing the old target and verifies the response returns the replacement target.
- Focused tests:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.existing-session-navigation-guard.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.existing-session.test.ts`
- Touched-file checks:
  - `oxfmt --check extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.existing-session-navigation-guard.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.existing-session-navigation-guard.test.ts`
  - `git diff --check`

## Live Existing-Session Browser Proof
Current head: `e809e5a2f8183fd683b66eabff185fe055d0f43c`.

I ran a local live proof with real Chrome, real `chrome-devtools-mcp@latest`, and the real OpenClaw Browser HTTP routes. The proof launched temporary `/usr/bin/google-chrome --headless=new --remote-debugging-port=<redacted>`, started `startBrowserBridgeServer` with an existing-session profile using `cdpUrl: http://127.0.0.1:<redacted>` and `ssrfPolicy: { dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork: true }`, then used only public Browser routes:

1. `POST /tabs/open` opened a launcher page.
2. `POST /act` with `kind: "evaluate"` opened a script-owned child tab.
3. `GET /snapshot?format=ai&targetId=<old>` captured refs from the child tab.
4. The child tab opened an same-URL replacement tab and closed itself after the guarded action passed URL stability checks.
5. `POST /act` ran each guarded action, and `POST /act` with `kind: "wait"` used the returned target to prove the next action succeeds.

Redacted live output summary:

```text
hover:          delay=1350 actStatus=200 old=chrome-mcp:<session>:...:5  returned=chrome-mcp:<session>:...:6  replaced=true waitStatus=200 waitOk=true
scrollIntoView: delay=1450 actStatus=200 old=chrome-mcp:<session>:...:11 returned=chrome-mcp:<session>:...:12 replaced=true waitStatus=200 waitOk=true
drag:           delay=1450 actStatus=200 old=chrome-mcp:<session>:...:7  returned=chrome-mcp:<session>:...:8  replaced=true waitStatus=200 waitOk=true
select:         delay=1350 actStatus=200 old=chrome-mcp:<session>:...:5  returned=chrome-mcp:<session>:...:6  replaced=true waitStatus=200 waitOk=true
fill:           delay=1350 actStatus=200 old=chrome-mcp:<session>:...:9  returned=chrome-mcp:<session>:...:10 replaced=true waitStatus=200 waitOk=true
```

This proof uses the real existing-session `/act` route for `hover`, `scrollIntoView`, `drag`, `select`, and `fill`; every success response returned a replacement target, and the immediate follow-up `wait` action succeeded on that returned target.

target.title: fix(codex): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox process execution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runProcess()` in the sandbox exec server listens on `child.stdout.on("data")` and `child.stderr.on("data")` but does not register `child.stdout.on("error")` / `child.stderr.on("error")` handlers. Node.js does not forward pipe stream errors to `child.on("error")` — an unhandled `error` event on a readable stream crashes the process with `ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR`. A broken sandbox stdout/stderr pipe takes down the codex sandbox exec server.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **`child.stdout.on("error")`**: preserve the failure message and kill the child with `SIGTERM`. Terminal notifications and backend finalization stay owned by the existing `child.once("close")` handler, so the process is never reported closed while the child is still running.
- **`child.stderr.on("error")`**: stderr is diagnostic-only; a broken stderr pipe must not kill a healthy process — logged via `embeddedAgentLog.warn`.

## User Impact

A broken sandbox stdout/stderr pipe no longer crashes the exec server. Stdout failures terminate the managed process through the normal close lifecycle; stderr failures are logged without disrupting execution.

## Evidence

**Realistic-stream regression** (`processes.stream-errors.test.ts`): `spawn` is mocked to return a child whose `stdout`/`stderr`/`stdin` are real `PassThrough` streams, driven through the production `startProcess` entry point. This exercises the real close path, including `finalizeProcess()` calling `stdin.destroy()` and `finalizeExec`.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.stream-errors.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**What the tests assert (after fix):**

1. **Stdout error → kill, then finalize via close:**
   - `managed.failure` is set; `child.kill("SIGTERM")` is called; `managed.closed` stays `false` and `finalizeExec` has NOT run yet (the error handler does not finalize).
   - After the real `close` event: `managed.closed` becomes `true`, `finalizeExec` runs exactly once with `status: "failed"`, and notifications are ordered `process/exited` before `process/closed`.
2. **Stderr error → warn only:** `embeddedAgentLog.warn` is called, `child.kill` is never called, the process stays alive, and `finalizeExec` does not run.

**Note on the prior revision:** the earlier fake child's `stdin` only implemented `end()`, so `finalizeProcess()`'s `stdin.destroy()` threw a `TypeError` that the close path swallowed — `finalizeExec` silently never ran even though the test passed. The `PassThrough` streams fix that: `finalizeExec` is now actually reached and asserted, so the finalization lifecycle is proven end-to-end.

**Static checks:** `oxlint` — exit 0; `oxfmt --check` — clean.

**What was not tested:** a live OS-level pipe failure (requires resource exhaustion). The error path itself is exercised exactly — the production handlers registered by `startProcess` receive real stream `error` events and the real close/finalize lifecycle runs to completion.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.stream-errors.test.ts` — 2/2 passed
- `oxlint` — exit 0; `oxfmt --check` — clean

AI-assisted.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: Add Cursor and filter widget provider options
target.body:
## Summary

- Add Cursor to configurable and interactive CodexBar widgets.
- Filter provider choices to widget-capable providers enabled in CodexBar settings, preserving settings order.
- Default new widgets to the first enabled supported provider, with a Codex fallback only when WidgetKit needs a valid choice.
- Keep persisted widget selections stable while preventing disabled providers from rendering retained usage data.
- Label legacy Cursor request quotas as `Requests`; label current Cursor quota rows as `Total`, `Auto`, and `API`.
- Add focused regression coverage and document the provider-choice, fallback, and disabled-state contracts.

Fixes #2040.

## Foundation

This keeps the existing widget snapshot and App Intents architecture:

- `ProviderChoice` remains the stable enum persisted by widget configurations.
- `EnabledProviderOptionsProvider` derives dynamic choices from `WidgetSnapshot.enabledProviders`.
- Unsupported providers are omitted through the existing `UsageProvider` to `ProviderChoice` mapping.
- `WidgetSnapshot.enabledEntry(for:)` is the shared eligibility gate for Usage, History, Metric, Switcher, and Burn Down surfaces, so retained entries remain available for re-enabling without leaking stale data while disabled.
- Before the first snapshot exists, all widget-capable providers remain available; if no enabled provider supports widgets, Codex is the configuration fallback.

## Verification

Exact candidate: `b45ccc21e5b3a46889c66c86c2913c9397ea2581`

- `swift test --filter WidgetSnapshotTests` — 21 tests passed across 3 suites.
- `swift test --filter CodexBarWidgetProviderTests` — 50 tests passed.
- `make check` — SwiftFormat and SwiftLint clean.
- `make test` — 601/601 selections passed across 51/51 groups; zero failures, retries, or timeouts.
- Structured review and source-blind behavior validation — clean/pass.
- Signed debug app and widget — strict code-sign verification passed; Gatekeeper accepted the Developer ID build.
- Live macOS 27 beta gallery — exact-head extension rendered Cursor before z.ai and showed `Total`, `Auto`, and `API` in small, medium, and large previews.
- Live placed-widget checks — small and medium switchers fit both provider chips plus all three quota rows; selection persisted across an exact extension-process restart.
- Live state checks — an all-disabled snapshot rendered the empty fallback instead of retained Cursor/Codex data; a legacy snapshot rendered `Requests` in every supported preview size.

Live screenshots were retained locally for verification and were not uploaded.

Thanks @Zihao-Qi for the contribution.

target.title: fix(web-media): add timeoutMs option to WebMediaOptions for remote fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadWebMedia` / `readRemoteMediaBuffer` had no upper bound on header-arrival latency. An unresponsive upstream could pin a Tlon media download or URL-backed image upload at the TCP/streaming-read layer until `readIdleTimeoutMs` finally tripped — and only if a body ever started. This PR threads a 15-minute header-arrival deadline through `WebMediaOptions` and the two Tlon call sites so a never-responding endpoint fails fast while slow-but-progressing transfers keep going.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial proposal exposed a new `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs?: number` (overall-request lifetime). ClawSweeper correctly rejected that as compatibility-breaking: it would have capped healthy bodies that keep yielding past 15 minutes. The narrower `FetchMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs` seam landed on `origin/main` via PR #103020 (merge commit `26aef8c48bc40d2ea456c2cfc3eca126dca33888`, 2026-07-10 13:31 UTC, currently reachable from `origin/main@bb26753705`) specifically for this stall class — header-only deadline via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`, `cleanup()`-ed once headers arrive so the body is not capped. This PR drops the parallel total-timeout surface and adopts that canonical seam end-to-end.

## What Changed

- `src/media/web-media.ts` — `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs?: number` removed; replaced with `WebMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs?: number`. `loadWebMediaInternal` destructures the new field and forwards it conditionally into `readRemoteMediaBuffer({ ..., responseHeaderTimeoutMs })` so an unset value does not overwrite main's "no header deadline" default.
- `src/media/web-media.test.ts` — replaces the prior "aborts a … via the overall timeoutMs deadline" test with **"forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs from loadWebMediaRaw through readRemoteMediaBuffer"** (using `vi.useFakeTimers()` + a progressing body stream, identical to main's `fetch.test.ts:438-485` "clears the response-header deadline while a healthy body keeps progressing" pattern). Asserts the resolved buffer contains the enqueued bytes after the header deadline clears — proving the public seam actually forwards the field.
- `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.ts` — replaces `TLON_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS` with `TLON_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000`; `downloadMedia`'s `fetchOptions` now forwards `responseHeaderTimeoutMs:` to both `saveRemoteMedia` and `readRemoteMediaBuffer`.
- `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.ts` — replaces `TLON_UPLOAD_IMAGE_TIMEOUT_MS` with `TLON_UPLOAD_IMAGE_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000`; `uploadImageFromUrl`'s `readRemoteMediaBuffer` call forwards the same.
- `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.test.ts`, `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.test.ts` — assertion relaxed to `expect.objectContaining({ ..., responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 15 * 60_000 })`.
- `proof-103206-tool-run.mts` — new live-run proof that exercises the canonical seam end-to-end (real stalled HTTP server + real `loadWebMedia` + real AbortSignal + surfaced error shape).

## User Impact

- Hard 15-minute upper bound on header-arrival latency for Tlon media downloads and URL-backed image uploads triggered by `extensions/tlon`.
- Healthy upstreams see no behavior change. **Slow-but-progressing transfers are explicitly NOT capped** — once headers arrive, the header deadline is cleared and `readIdleTimeoutMs` (30s for Tlon) continues to bound chunk gaps. This is the deliberate behavior change vs. the prior total-timeout proposal.
- Tlon users on very slow networks where headers legitimately take >15 min will see new failures. This matches the existing 15-minute ceiling from canonical precedent #103266 (`src/cli/nodes-camera.ts:20`, `CAMERA_URL_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS`); the trade-off has already been accepted by maintainers on that merge.

## Evidence

### Live behavior proof (real HTTP server, real fetch, real AbortSignal, surfaced error shape)

Local fallback run (Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-103206-tool-run.mts
[proof] stalled HTTP server listening on http://127.0.0.1:36539
[proof] calling loadWebMedia with responseHeaderTimeoutMs=1000ms (production code path uses 15*60_000)
[proof] this exercises the canonical seam from PR #103020:
[proof]   loadWebMedia -> readRemoteMediaBuffer -> fetchGuardedMediaResponse
[proof]   -> fetchWithSsrFGuard -> buildTimeoutAbortSignal (response header deadline)
[proof]   -> globalThis.fetch
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 1000ms (elapsed 1001ms) operation=media response headers url=http://127.0.0.1:36539/never-responds.png
[proof] elapsed: 1154ms
[proof] surfaced error.name: MediaFetchError
[proof] surfaced error.code: fetch_failed
[proof] surfaced error.message: Failed to fetch media from http://127.0.0.1:36539/never-responds.png: request timed out
[proof] surfaced error.cause.name: TimeoutError
[proof] surfaced error.cause.message: request timed out
[proof] result: responseHeaderTimeoutMs fired through real production path
{
  "url": "http://127.0.0.1:36539/never-responds.png",
  "responseHeaderTimeoutMs": 1000,
  "outcome": {
    "kind": "error",
    "name": "MediaFetchError",
    "code": "fetch_failed",
    "message": "Failed to fetch media from http://127.0.0.1:36539/never-responds.png: request timed out",
    "causeName": "TimeoutError",
    "causeMessage": "request timed out",
    "elapsedMs": 1154
  },
  "passed": true
}
```

Key observations:
- **1154ms elapsed** (vs 1000ms `responseHeaderTimeoutMs`): the `[fetch-timeout]` log fires at the deadline, proving the AbortSignal fires at the configured header deadline.
- **Surfaced error shape**: `MediaFetchError { code: "fetch_failed", cause: TimeoutError("request timed out") }` — the exact error shape that propagates to the Tlon extension caller.

### Repository test (forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs through the public seam)

Added in `src/media/web-media.test.ts > loadWebMedia > forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs from loadWebMediaRaw through readRemoteMediaBuffer`. The test uses `vi.useFakeTimers()` and an `enqueue([1],25) → enqueue([2],50) → close(75)` body stream (matching main's pattern at `fetch.test.ts:438-485`). Asserts the resolved buffer equals the concatenation of enqueued bytes — proving the header deadline is cleared on success and the body keeps progressing past it.

Focused suite runs (local fallback — Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media/web-media.test.ts src/media/fetch.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  121 passed (121)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.test.ts extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

### Canonical precedents

- **PR #103020 / merge `26aef8c48bc40d2ea456c2cfc3eca126dca33888`** — `FetchMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs` at `src/media/fetch.ts:82`; the canonical seam. Implements header-only deadline via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`, `cleanup()`-ed on success so the body is not capped.
- **PR #103266 / merge `541c9f0bf01712d81d5217eb2a5c15d05686259d`** — canonical 15-minute bounded-media ceiling from `src/cli/nodes-camera.ts:20`. This PR reuses the same ceiling on the narrower header-only deadline.
- **Telegram precedent** — `extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.resolve-media-retry.ts:356` already uses `TELEGRAM_DOWNLOAD_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000`. This PR's constant names mirror that pattern.

## Coordination with #103209

With the canonical seam now on `origin/main`, both this PR and #103209 independently use that seam — they no longer duplicate each other and either can land in any order. No cross-repo stacking required. Each branch typechecks standalone; the `forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs from loadWebMediaRaw through readRemoteMediaBuffer` test on this branch and the equivalent proof path on #103209 cover the same end-to-end contract from different call sites (Tlon vs. agent-tools).

target.title: fix(shell): resolve pwsh.exe/.cmd/.bat on PATH for Windows shell discovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, PowerShell 7 delivered via the Microsoft Store / App Execution Alias (and most portable installs) ships as `pwsh.exe`. `resolvePowerShellPath()` step 3 calls `resolveShellFromPath("pwsh")`, which only probed a **bare** `pwsh` with no extension. `fs.accessSync(entry/pwsh)` therefore returned `ENOENT`, so shell discovery fell through to Windows PowerShell 5.1 instead of using pwsh 7. This is the actual Windows pwsh resolution gap (distinct from the custom-shell `-c` args discussion in #104053).

## Evidence

Local reproduction on this Windows host (PowerShell 7.6.3 present only as the Store `pwsh.exe` alias, no `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7`):
- `fs.accessSync("...\pwsh")` -> `ENOENT` (bare name missed by discovery)
- `fs.accessSync("...\pwsh.exe")` -> `OK` (extension probe hits it)
- After the fix, `resolveShellFromPath("pwsh")` returns the `pwsh.exe` path on PATH, and `resolvePowerShellPath()` prefers pwsh 7 over the 5.1 fallback.

This matches the source-level analysis: current main only looks for a bare `pwsh`, so a PATH entry containing only `pwsh.exe` is skipped before the Windows PowerShell 5.1 fallback (noted by the ClawSweeper review). The PR also adds Windows-only regression tests (guarded by `isWin` so Linux CI is unaffected): finds `pwsh.exe` when a bare `pwsh` is absent, prefers a bare `pwsh` match over `pwsh.exe` when both exist, and `resolvePowerShellPath()` resolves `pwsh.exe` on PATH instead of 5.1.

(Private paths and credentials redacted; this is a local OpenClaw gateway host.)

## Root cause

`resolveShellFromPath` joined the entry with the bare name and never tried executable extensions on Windows:

```ts
const candidate = path.join(entry, name); // only "pwsh", never "pwsh.exe"
```

## Fix

On `win32`, also probe `.exe`, mirroring the existing pattern already used by `resolveWindowsBashPath` (`"bash.exe"` / `"bash"`).

```ts
const executableExtensions = process.platform === "win32" ? [".exe"] : [];
const candidates = [base, ...executableExtensions.map((ext) => base + ext)];
```

**Scope note (addressed ClawSweeper review):** only `.exe` is added. `.cmd`/`.bat` are intentionally excluded because PTY execution (`createPtyAdapter`) spawns the resolved shell directly without child mode's `cmd.exe` wrapping, so a `pwsh.cmd` selected here could be chosen and then fail in PTY mode. `.exe` is directly executable in both child and PTY modes. Non-Windows behavior is unchanged.

This makes a Store/portable `pwsh.exe` discoverable on PATH, so `resolvePowerShellPath()` prefers pwsh 7 over 5.1.

## Test plan

Windows-only tests in `shell-utils.test.ts` (guarded by `isWin` so Linux CI is unaffected):
- finds `pwsh.exe` when a bare `pwsh` is absent
- prefers a bare `pwsh` match over `pwsh.exe` when both exist
- `resolvePowerShellPath()` resolves `pwsh.exe` on PATH instead of 5.1 when standard install dirs are empty

Existing tests unchanged; non-Windows `resolveShellFromPath` behavior preserved.

target.title: fix(agents): add size limit to LSP message parser
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The LSP message parser accepted unbounded `Content-Length`
values. A malicious or misbehaving LSP server could send an arbitrarily
large `Content-Length` header, causing unbounded buffer allocation and
memory exhaustion. Additionally, a very long decimal `Content-Length`
(e.g., 400+ digits) causes `Number.parseInt` to return `Infinity`, which
was stored as an infinite drain counter — permanently suppressing all
future LSP output and leaving pending requests to time out.

**Root cause**: When `Content-Length` exceeded the 10 MB limit, the parser
only skipped the header + separator bytes but kept the declared body in
`session.buffer`. If the oversized body arrived across multiple stream
chunks, the buffer would grow unboundedly. For non-safe integer lengths
(`Infinity` from `parseInt`), the arithmetic computed `bodyStart + Infinity
= Infinity`, storing an infinite `oversizeDrainRemaining` that never
decrements. Additionally, when the final drain chunk exactly matched the
remaining byte count, the handler returned early without failing the
session, leaving the pending request to time out.

**Solution**: Add a 10 MB `Content-Length` limit that fully drains the
declared oversized body when the frame is completely buffered, or tracks
remaining bytes to skip via `session.oversizeDrainRemaining` when the body
arrives across chunks. Non-safe integer Content-Length values (Infinity)
are detected before drain arithmetic and signal a fatal protocol error.
Finite oversized frames (>10 MB but still a safe integer) trigger session
failure after dispatching any valid responses parsed before the oversized
frame — the associated pending request is rejected immediately instead of
waiting for the normal request timeout. The exact-match drain completion
boundary (`raw.length === oversizeDrainRemaining`) now falls through to
the session failure check instead of returning early.

**What changed**: `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts`
- `parseLspMessages`: accepts optional `oversizeDrainRemaining` out-param
  with `fatal` flag; on oversized frames drains the full frame or signals
  remaining bytes and sets the fatal flag. On non-safe integer
  Content-Length signals a fatal condition via NaN.
- `handleIncomingData`: drains `session.oversizeDrainRemaining` from raw
  stream data before appending to the parse buffer. Detects non-finite
  drain remaining or drained finite oversized frames and calls
  `failLspSession` after dispatching any completed responses parsed
  before the bad header. Fixed the exact-match drain boundary: changed
  `<=` to `<` so the exact-match case continues into session failure.
- `LspSession` type: added `oversizeDrainRemaining: number`,
  `oversizeDrainSeen: boolean`

**What did NOT change**: Valid message parsing, session lifecycle, tool
materialization — all unchanged for frames within the 10 MB limit.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: LSP message parser now closes three gaps:
1) fully drains finite oversized Content-Length frames (>10 MB) to
prevent memory exhaustion, 2) fails the session for non-safe integer
Content-Length (Infinity from parseInt) instead of permanently suppressing
all future LSP output, and 3) fails the session for finite oversized
frames after dispatching any valid responses parsed before the oversized
frame so the associated pending request is rejected immediately instead
of timing out.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22.19.0, pnpm 11.2.2

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 18 tests pass, including 4 new
handler-level tests for finite oversized Content-Length session failure.

**Before-fix behavior (if applicable)**: Finite oversized frames (>10 MB)
were silently drained without failing the session, leaving the associated
pending request to time out after 10 seconds instead of failing
immediately. When the final drain chunk exactly matched the remaining
oversized body bytes, the handler returned early with a zero counter
without failing the session.

**After-fix evidence**:

All 18 tests pass:
```text
 ✓ bundle LSP runtime > oversized Content-Length handling (2)
 ✓ bundle LSP runtime > unsafe Content-Length handling (4)
 ✓ bundle LSP runtime > finite oversized Content-Length handling (4)
   ✓ sets fatal flag on parseLspMessages oversizeDrain
   ✓ fails LSP session on finite oversized frame through runtime handler path
   ✓ dispatches valid response before failing session on finite oversized frame
   ✓ fails the session when the final drain chunk exactly completes
```

**Real LSP server evidence**:

Tested against `vscode-json-languageserver` via stdio:

**Terminal output**:
```text
============================================================
L2 EVIDENCE: Real LSP server session via Content-Length framing
Server: vscode-json-languageserver
============================================================
Frame #1: {
  "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "capabilities": {
      "textDocumentSync": 2, "hoverProvider": true,
      "documentSymbolProvider": true, "foldingRangeProvider": true,
      "selectionRangeProvider": true
    }
  }
}
Frame #2: { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "result": null }
----------------------------------------
Initialize returned capabilities: ✅
Completion responded: ✅
CONCLUSION: Real LSP server session works end-to-end ✅
```

This proves the LSP message parser correctly handles real server I/O
with proper Content-Length framing.

**What was not tested**: A real LSP server sending non-safe Content-Length
or oversized (>10 MB) values — these are protocol violations that no
well-behaved LSP server would produce. The code paths are exercised
through handler-level tests that use the identical `handleIncomingData`
path the production LSP session uses.

**Risk level**: Low — non-safe and finite oversized Content-Length values
both trigger session failure after dispatching valid responses. All
existing message sizes within the 10 MB limit use the unchanged happy
path. merge-risk: low

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — 10 MB is well above realistic LSP message sizes
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — all 18 tests pass
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation — no docs changes needed
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary — none

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Brave web search accepted configured API keys, but env-backed SecretRefs in `tools.web.search.apiKey` were not resolved through the shared web-search credential path before falling back to `BRAVE_API_KEY`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Brave provider should treat direct API keys, env SecretRefs, and provider fallback env vars consistently with the shared web-search credential contract. This change routes Brave credential resolution through the existing shared resolver instead of duplicating a literal-only read.

## User Impact

Users can configure Brave web search with an env SecretRef and have it used without live-key tests or custom provider-auth behavior. Existing `BRAVE_API_KEY` fallback behavior remains intact.

## Evidence

- Changed `extensions/brave/src/brave-web-search-provider.runtime.ts`.
- Added a regression in `extensions/brave/src/brave-web-search-provider.test.ts` proving a configured env SecretRef supplies the request auth header ahead of `BRAVE_API_KEY`.
- Live open-PR conflict scan found no exact overlap on these touched files.

## Proof

- Rebased cleanly onto `upstream/main` at `fbcb7812cb`.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/brave/src/brave-web-search-provider.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose`
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`
- Earlier touched-file checks: `pnpm format:check`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json ...`, and Claude autoreview clean after Codex autoreview was blocked by local OpenAI API 401.
